summary: Hector climbs the Stormbreaker to manually adjust a microscopic cable misalignment amidst a lethal geomagnetic storm.
text:
"It's not just a storm," Hector yelled over the wind. "It's a battery! A big, angry, floating battery!"

He was strapped to the top of the Stormbreaker tower, fifty meters above the Enclave. The wind tore at his goggles, screaming like a jet engine. Below him, the Enclave was safe in the bunker. The clouds above weren't grey; they were a bruised, violent purple, lit from within by constant sheet lightning. The air tasted of ozone and copper. He was looking for the step leader—the invisible path of ionized air that preceded the main strike. They were employing real-time Lorenz strange-attractor bifurcation targeting, firing millisecond pre-strike ionization pulses to lock chaotic lightning onto the collector rods at 98% efficiency.

"The coupling," Hector muttered, panic rising. "The coupling is 0.5 degrees off vertical. The inductance will be asymmetrical."

He fumbled with his harness, his hands trembling. The kinetic joy of the storm evaporated, replaced by an agonizing, pinpoint obsession with the copper bracket. The asymmetry would cause a harmonic wobble in the containment geode's magnetic field. He had to align it. He had to make it perfect. He hauled himself upward, ignoring the static charge raising the hairs on his arms. The wind tried to tear him from the ladder, but he locked his grip, reaching the massive collector node. He stared at the offending bolt, the half-degree variance glaring like a beacon in the storm.

He yanked his torque wrench from his belt. He didn't just need to survive the storm; he needed to master it, down to the millimeter. He applied pressure, the metal groaning against his strength. The bolt shifted, the coupling snapping perfectly vertical just as the sky erupted. A blinding pillar of white fire slammed into the rod, the concussive force vibrating through his bones.

"Hector, you absolute lunatic, get down here!" Kaio's voice cracked over the comms, breathless and urgent. "The lower perimeter sensors are tripping!"
